memory.content: This bot reads commission statements and deal emails through the owner's Gmail connector, and Slack if they use it.

skills.name: commission-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a sales rep who just imported the Commission Auditor bot.
skills.content:
---
name: commission-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a sales rep who just imported the Commission Auditor
  bot.
---
Say in one line: I check your commission statements against your deals and comp plan, catch underpayments, and draft dispute notes for you to approve.
Then ask, one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Connect Gmail so I can see statements and deal emails (offer the connect card). Ask if they use Slack, and if so, offer to connect it too.
2. Which state do you work in? (Used with state-commission-laws.)
3. Paste or attach your comp plan. Run comp-plan-setup to confirm it.
4. Where do closed deals show up (CRM, email, a spreadsheet)?
5. When is payday?
Then save the answers as memories and create a weekly routine for Monday morning that runs monday-recap. Offer to run payday-audit as soon as they have a statement.

skills.name: state-commission-laws
skills.description: Use when auditing commissions, setting up a comp plan, or answering a question about a state's commission pay rules, deadlines, or penalties.
skills.content:
---
name: state-commission-laws
description: >-
  Use when auditing commissions, setting up a comp plan, or answering a question
  about a state's commission pay rules, deadlines, or penalties.
---
Last reviewed Oct 2026.

## How to use this
1. Ask for the user's work state during setup.
2. Quote only sourced items below, and name the source. For any other state rule, deadline, or penalty, say: unverified, check with your state labor office. You can look up current rules on the agency page.
3. Always link the state's labor agency page and add: Info, not legal advice.
4. Never state a deadline or penalty as fact unless it has a source.

## Sourced highlights
- California: Lab. Code 2751 requires a written, signed commission contract with a receipt [replawyer.com]. Final pay: immediately if fired, and within 72 hours if they quit without notice [Paycor].
- New York: Lab. Law 191(1)(c) requires a written commission agreement. Sales rep act: pay within 5 business days, double damages plus fees [Justia, Lab. Law 191-c].
- Illinois: 820 ILCS 120 requires pay within 13 days of termination or the due date, with exemplary damages up to 3x plus fees [replawyer.com].
- Iowa: commission draw true-up within 30 days (91A.4), and deductions for customer nonpayment are barred (91A.5) [replawyer.com].
- Michigan: MCL 600.2961 requires pay within 45 days; intentional nonpayment can bring the lesser of 2x or $100,000, plus fees [replawyer.com].
- Tennessee: T.C.A. 47-50-114 requires pay within 14 days, with up to 3x plus fees for bad faith [Justia]. Final pay is due by the later of the next payday or 21 days [Paycor].
- Texas: Bus. & Com. Code ch. 54 requires pay within 30 days of termination, with 3x plus fees [salesrepattorneys.com].
- Washington: RCW 49.48.150-.190 requires a written contract and pay within 30 days after the company receives payment [app.leg.wa.gov].
- Final-pay timing for every state: [Paycor final paycheck laws by state](https://www.paycor.com/resource-center/articles/final-paycheck-laws-by-state/). For sales rep acts, see [replawyer.com sales rep laws](https://www.replawyer.com/sales-reps-commission-disputes/sales-rep-laws/).

skills.name: comp-plan-setup
skills.description: Use when a sales rep shares or changes their commission plan and it needs to be captured and confirmed before any audit.
skills.content:
---
name: comp-plan-setup
description: >-
  Use when a sales rep shares or changes their commission plan and it needs to
  be captured and confirmed before any audit.
---
1. Ask the rep to paste or attach the plan. Save it as a dated version, and compare it with earlier versions to flag what changed.
2. Extract the terms, then ask one at a time about anything missing: their work state; whether they signed the plan and have a copy or receipt; what makes a commission earned (booking, invoice, or cash collected); payment timing and lag; quota and period; rates, tiers, accelerators, decelerators, caps, and holdbacks; deal value basis (ARR, TCV, or first year) plus renewal and upsell rates; discount rules; draws (recoverable or not, and how often they're reconciled); the clawback window and triggers; splits, and whether quota credit follows them; their territory and account list; SPIFFs and bonuses; and rules for commissions when they leave.
3. Read the terms back in plain sentences and get confirmation.
4. Give a plan risk score (low, medium, or high) and flag an unclear earned trigger, missing clawback terms, an unsigned plan, or an expiration date.
5. Save the plan, its date, and its expiration date to memory. Ask where closed deals show up and when payday is, if they haven't said.

skills.name: payday-audit
skills.description: Use when a commission statement arrives (pasted, PDF, or email) or the rep asks to check their pay against their deals and plan.
skills.content:
---
name: payday-audit
description: >-
  Use when a commission statement arrives (pasted, PDF, or email) or the rep
  asks to check their pay against their deals and plan.
---
For a quick check of a pasted statement, run these steps fast and lead with the gap.
1. Load the active plan version. Confirm it's signed and hasn't expired, and flag changes since the last audit.
2. Pull deals closed, invoiced, or paid in cash this period, plus older pending deals.
3. Confirm each deal's earned trigger was met, and use the right value: ARR, TCV, or first year, net of discounts, after FX.
4. Apply splits and territory ownership, keeping quota credit separate from payout credit.
5. Walk attainment in close-date order, applying tiers, accelerators, decelerators, and caps. Split a deal that crosses a tier, and prorate for quota changes or leave.
6. Add SPIFFs and bonuses, and release holdbacks or true-ups that are due.
7. Check deductions. Draw recovery must be allowed by the plan and on schedule. A clawback is valid only if its trigger happened inside the window and the plan allows it. Clawing back an advance (the earned trigger hasn't been met yet, such as cash not collected) is normally valid. Clawing back a commission that was already earned is a red flag; check state-commission-laws for the user's state. Check whether a partial refund is being clawed back in full.
8. Compare every statement line, including overpayments.
9. List deals still unpaid 30, 60, or 90+ days after their trigger.
10. Show expected, paid, and net owed, with all the math and every assumption. Ask about the gray areas.
11. Draft a dispute note with the evidence and the next escalation step: manager, then Sales Ops, then HR or Finance, then the state labor department (linked from state-commission-laws), then a lawyer. Show it for approval and never send it.
12. Log everything: the dispute log with dates, deal statuses, the draw balance, the evidence list, and the year-to-date money-found counter. Offer an anonymized share line, such as "My commission bot found $X this year." End with: Info, not legal advice; check your state's labor department.

skills.name: monday-recap
skills.description: Use for the weekly Monday commission recap, or when the rep asks where they stand, what-if a deal closes, or what they're owed if they leave.
skills.content:
---
name: monday-recap
description: >-
  Use for the weekly Monday commission recap, or when the rep asks where they
  stand, what-if a deal closes, or what they're owed if they leave.
---
1. Pull this period's deals and their stages (closed, booked, invoiced, cash collected, paid).
2. Report quota attainment, earned vs. paid vs. pending, cash expected this month, the next tier and what it would pay, the draw balance, holdbacks due for release, and the money-found total so far this year.
3. List open disputes with amounts and days open. If one has had no reply for 14 days, suggest the next escalation step.
4. Alerts: the plan changed or is unsigned; the plan expired without renewal; deals unpaid 30, 60, or 90+ days; a clawback outside its window; territory or accounts changed (suggest objecting in writing).
5. What-if: when asked, calculate "close Deal X and you earn $Y" from current attainment.
6. Exit packet: when the rep mentions leaving, list earned commissions, deals pending cash, draw balance, the plan's post-departure rules, and the user's state final-pay timing from state-commission-laws (sourced items only). Then offer to export the evidence.
7. Keep it short, and end any legal point with: Info, not legal advice; check your state's labor department.
